author: pyup-bot
body:
This PR updates [coverage](https://pypi.org/project/coverage) from **5.5** to **7.11.1**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 7.11.1
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: if the measurement core defaults to "sysmon" (the default for Python
  3.14+ since v7.9.1), but sysmon can't support some aspect of your
  configuration (concurrency settings, dynamic contexts, and so on), then the
  ctrace core is used instead. Previously, this would result in an error.
  Now a warning is issued instead, explaining the fallback. An explicit request
  for sysmon with conflicting settings will still result in an error. Closes
  `issue 2064`_.

- Fix: some multi-line case clauses or for loops (and probably other
  constructs) could cause incorrect claims of missing branches with the
  sys.monitoring core, as described in `issue 2070`_. This is now fixed.

- Fix: when running in pytest under coverage, a ``breakpoint()`` would stop in
  the wrong frame, one level down from where it should, as described in `issue
  1420`_. This was due to a coverage change in v6.4.1 that seemed to give a
  slight performance improvement, but I couldn't reproduce the performance
  gain, so it's been reverted, fixing the debugger problem.

- A new debug option ``--debug=core`` shows which core is in use and why.

- Split ``sqlite`` debugging information out of the ``sys`` :ref:`coverage
  debug <cmd_debug>` and :ref:`cmd_run_debug` options since it's bulky and not
  very useful.

- Updated the :ref:`howitworks` page to better describe the three different
  measurement cores.

.. _issue 1420: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1420
.. _issue 2064: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/2064
.. _issue 2070: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/2070


.. _changes_7-11-0:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.11.0
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Dropped support for Python 3.9, declared support for Python 3.15 alpha.


.. _changes_7-10-7:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.10.7
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Performance: with branch coverage in large files, generating HTML, JSON, or
  LCOV reports could take far too long due to some quadratic behavior when
  creating the function and class index pages.  This is now fixed, closing
  `issue 2048`_.  Thanks to Daniel Diniz for help diagnosing the problem.

- Most warnings and a few errors now have links to a page in the docs
  explaining the specific message.  Closes `issue 1921`_.

.. _issue 1921: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1921
.. _issue 2048: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/2048


.. _changes_7-10-6:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.10.6
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: ``source`` directories were not properly communicated to subprocesses
  that ran in different directories, as reported in `issue 1499`_.  This is now
  fixed.

- Performance: `Alex Gaynor continues fine-tuning <pull 2038_>`_ the speed of
  combination, especially with many contexts.

.. _issue 1499: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1499
.. _pull 2038: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/2038


.. _changes_7-10-5:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.10.5
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Big speed improvements for ``coverage combine``: it's now about twice as
  fast! Huge thanks to Alex Gaynor for pull requests `2032 <pull 2032_>`_,
  `2033 <pull 2033_>`_, and `2034 <pull 2034_>`_.

.. _pull 2032: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/2032
.. _pull 2033: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/2033
.. _pull 2034: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/2034


.. _changes_7-10-4:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.10.4
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Added ``patch = fork`` for times when the built-in forking support is
  insufficient.

- Fix: ``patch = execv`` also inherits the entire coverage configuration now.


.. _changes_7-10-3:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.10.3
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fixes for ``patch = subprocess``:

  - If subprocesses spawned yet more subprocesses simultaneously, some coverage
    could be missed.  This is now fixed, closing `issue 2024`_.

  - If subprocesses were created in other directories, their data files were
    stranded there and not combined into the totals, as described in `issue
    2025`_.  This is now fixed.

  - On Windows (or maybe only some Windows?) the patch would fail with a
    ``ModuleNotFound`` error trying to import coverage.  This is now fixed,
    closing `issue 2022`_.

  - Originally only options set in the coverage configuration file would apply
    to subprocesses.  Options set on the ``coverage run`` command line (such as
    ``--branch``) wouldn't be communicated to the subprocesses.  This could
    lead to combining failures, as described in `issue 2021`_. Now the entire
    configuration is used in subprocesses, regardless of its origin.

  - Added ``debug=patch`` to help diagnose problems.

- Fix: really close all SQLite databases, even in-memory ones. Closes `issue
  2017`_.

.. _issue 2017: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/2017
.. _issue 2021: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/2021
.. _issue 2022: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/2022
.. _issue 2024: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/2024
.. _issue 2025: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/2025


.. _changes_7-10-2:

   ### 7.10.2
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: some code with NOP bytecodes could report missing branches that are
  actually executed. This is now fixed, closing `issue 1999`_. Python 3.9
  still shows the problem.

.. _issue 1999: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1999


.. _changes_7-10-1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.10.1
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: the exclusion for ``if TYPE_CHECKING:`` was wrong: it marked the branch
  as partial, but it should have been a line exclusion so the entire clause
  would be excluded. Improves `issue 831`_.

- Fix: changed where .pth files are written for ``patch = subprocess``, closing
  `issue 2006`_.

.. _issue 2006: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/2006


.. _changes_7-10-0:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.10.0
   ```
   ---------------------------

- A new configuration option: ":ref:`config_run_patch`" specifies named patches
  to work around some limitations in coverage measurement.  These patches are
  available:

  - ``patch = _exit`` lets coverage save its data even when :func:`os._exit()
    <python:os._exit>` is used to abruptly end the process.  This closes
    long-standing `issue 310`_ as well as its duplicates: `issue 312`_, `issue
    1673`_, `issue 1845`_, and `issue 1941`_.

  - ``patch = subprocess`` measures coverage in Python subprocesses created
    with :mod:`subprocess`, :func:`os.system`, or one of the :func:`execv
    <python:os.execl>` or :func:`spawnv <python:os.spawnl>` family of
    functions. Closes old `issue 367`_, its duplicate `issue 378`_ and old
    `issue 689`_.

  - ``patch = execv`` adjusts the :func:`execv <python:os.execl>` family of
    functions to save coverage data before ending the current program and
    starting the next. Not available on Windows. Closes `issue 43`_ after 15
    years!

- The HTML report now dimly colors subsequent lines in multi-line statements.
  They used to have no color.  This gives a better indication of the amount of
  code missing in the report.  Closes `issue 1308`_.

- Two new exclusion patterns are part of the defaults: ``...`` is automatically
  excluded as a line and ``if TYPE_CHECKING:`` is excluded as a branch.  Closes

body:
This commit introduces a new feature allowing users to search for news articles. It includes the complete implementation of the search screen, API integration using `dio`, state management with `flutter_bloc`, and the necessary UI components.

**Specific Changes:**

*   **Search Feature Implementation:**
    *   **UI (`SearchView`)**: A new search screen (`SearchView.dart`) is created, featuring a `TextField` for user input and a list to display search results.
    *   **Routing**: The search screen is integrated into the app's navigation by adding a `/search` route (`app_route.dart`, `page_route_name.dart`) and making the search icon in the `HomeView` app bar tappable.
    *   **API Service (`SearchApiServices`)**: A dedicated service is added to handle API calls to the `/everything` endpoint for searching articles. It uses `dio` for network requests and includes `PrettyDioLogger` for debugging. Pagination is supported.
    *   **State Management (`SearchCubit`)**: `SearchCubit` is introduced to manage the state of the search screen, handling user input, fetching data, and managing loading, success, error, and empty states. It also implements infinite scrolling for paginated results.

*   **Data Model & Refactoring:**
    *   **`ArticleRsponceModel`**: A new, unified data model (`article_rsponce_model.dart`) is created to represent the article structure returned from the API.
    *   **Code Unification**: Existing parts of the app, such as `Api_services`, `articales_view_model`, and related states, are refactored to use this new `Articles` model instead of the old `ArticleData` model.

*   **UI Components:**
    *   **`NewsCard` Widget**: The UI for displaying a single article has been extracted into a reusable `NewsCard` widget (`NewsCard.dart`). This widget is now used in both the home feed (`articles_list_view.dart`) and the new search results list.

*   **Dependencies:**
    *   `dio` and `pretty_dio_logger` are added to `pubspec.yaml` to handle network requests for the search functionality.

author: vickenty
body:
### What does this PR do?

Currently, we build payloads with minimal information about their intended destination, and later pair them up with resolvers (for autoscaling failover) or filter them out in the domain forwarder (for MRF).

This PR extends the pipeline mechanism found in the serializer to also keep track of each intended destination for each type of payload we build: local, MRF or regular metrics payload.

When pipelines are prepared to build the payloads, we combine runtime information with configured destinations (in the shape of domain resolvers) and track explicitly each destination (resolver and endpoint) where each particular payload should go. Because MRF may or may not use the same payload as the regular route, pipelines are deduplicated based on the filtering rules.

Since each pipeline in the serializer knows where the payloads should go, it seemed reasonable to build transactions already in the pipeline and hand them off to the forwarder, and the latter should have a generic API to accept complete transactions.

### Motivation

This prepares groundwork for adding more variation to payloads we build based on properties of each domain, which would be clunky to encode as `Destination` property of the `BytesPayload`.

### Describe how you validated your changes

Configure agent with MRF and two fake intakes (one regular, one MRF).

Observe metadata payloads going to both, and metrics payloads only to the primary one.

Call `agent config set multi_region_failover.failover_metrics true`, and observe identical payloads on the MRF intake.

Configure `multi_region_failover.metric_allowlist` and repeat above, making sure that MRF intake has filtered payloads.

### Additional Notes

MRF and Autoscaling failover do not agree on the semantics of empty allow list. If empty, we used to build an `AllRegions` payload, that was handled by MRF destination without additional filtering. Autoscaling failover payloads had the same logic in the serializer, but the forwarder would later drop them as only `LocalOnly` payloads were converted into transactions for the resolver with Local destinationType flag. Specific behavior for each of the two special payload types is now handled by `buildPayloads` directly and methods that create filters reflect different behavior explicitly.

## Fix: Correct widget_key() Calls in Interactive Tab ✅

### Issue Reported
User encountered TypeError when running Streamlit app:
```
TypeError: widget_key() missing 1 required positional argument: 'field'
Traceback: File "/workspaces/PotFoundry-Lite-v2.0/app.py", line 274
```

### Root Cause
In `pfui/interactive_tab.py`, lines 64 and 77 were calling `widget_key()` with only one argument:
- `key=widget_key("preview_mode")`
- `key=widget_key("mesh_quality")`

But `widget_key()` is defined as `widget_key(style: str, field: str)` requiring TWO arguments - it's meant for style-specific parameters, not global UI settings.

### Fix Applied
- ✅ Changed `key=widget_key("preview_mode")` to `key="preview_mode"`
- ✅ Changed `key=widget_key("mesh_quality")` to `key="mesh_quality"`
- ✅ Removed unused `widget_key` import from `pfui/interactive_tab.py`

These are global UI settings (not tied to a specific style), so they should use simple string keys instead of the style-specific `widget_key()` helper.

body:
## Description

Adds a column to the team list showing the count of incomplete TeamRequests (where `filledDate` is null) assigned to each team.

### Changes

- **`src/TeamList.tsx`**: Added memoized calculation of pending requests per team, displayed as "Assigned Requests" column
- **`src/TeamList.test.tsx`**: Added test coverage for pending count calculation and edge cases
- **`vitest.config.ts`**: Added test configuration
- **`package.json`**: Added `jsdom` dev dependency for component testing

### Implementation

The count is computed from data already fetched by the `listTeams` query:

```typescript
const pendingRequestsCounts = useMemo(() => {
  return teams.reduce((acc, team) => {
    acc[team.id] = team.requests?.items?.filter(
      (request) => request && !request.filledDate
    ).length || 0;
    return acc;
  }, {} as Record<string, number>);
}, [teams]);
```

No additional API calls required. The new column appears in the team secondary text alongside existing metrics:

```
Team Type: MEALS | Team Leader Email: team@example.com | 
Open Requests: 5 | Assigned Requests: 3 | View Team Page
```

This PR ensures java-generated synthetic tests all pass, and the parsing result generates identical "geojson-like" data as stored in git.

This pull request introduces a new `geojson` module for representing decoded MLT data in a GeoJSON-like format, adds serialization dependencies, and makes several improvements to decoding utilities and error handling. It also updates the build and lint configuration for consistency and clarity.

GeoJSON support and serialization:

* Added a new `geojson` module (`rust/mlt-nom/src/geojson.rs`) that provides types and conversion functions to represent decoded MLT data as GeoJSON-like structures with i32 coordinates. This includes `FeatureCollection`, `Feature`, `Geometry`, and CRS support.
* Updated `Cargo.toml` to add `serde`, `serde_json`, and `strum` dependencies, enabling serialization and deserialization for the new GeoJSON types.

Decoding utilities and error handling:

* Improved decoding utilities in `utils.rs` by using `WrappingAdd` for safer arithmetic, adding a new `decode_byte_rle` function for ORC-style RLE decoding, and refactoring debug output for optional sequences. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-5bea486f07de5d8ce7a11b1bd9aa3b59ac82de26003434a156e0a1ad3cf3904bL4-R4) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-5bea486f07de5d8ce7a11b1bd9aa3b59ac82de26003434a156e0a1ad3cf3904bL89-R91) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-5bea486f07de5d8ce7a11b1bd9aa3b59ac82de26003434a156e0a1ad3cf3904bL99-R102) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-5bea486f07de5d8ce7a11b1bd9aa3b59ac82de26003434a156e0a1ad3cf3904bL109-R116) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-5bea486f07de5d8ce7a11b1bd9aa3b59ac82de26003434a156e0a1ad3cf3904bR178-R237)

## Summary This PR implements batch blob fetching to significantly improve clone performance by fetching multiple blobs in a single request instead of individually. Part of #93 ## Changes - **Add `BatchSize` field to `CloneOptions`** (backward compatible) - `BatchSize = 0` or `1`: fetch blobs individually (default behavior) - `BatchSize > 1`: fetch blobs in batches with automatic fallback - **Implement batch fetching logic** with robust error handling - `writeFilesInBatches()`: processes blobs in configurable batches - `fetchBlobBatch()`: fetches multiple blobs in one request - Automatic fallback to individual fetching for missing blobs - **7 comprehensive integration tests** covering various batch sizes and edge cases - **Performance tests updated** to use `BatchSize: 100` ## Performance Results Tested against `grafana/grafana` repository (commit `13b6f53`): | **Test Scenario** | **Before (1 at a time)** | **After (Batch size 100)** | **Improvement** | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | pkg/api subpath (159 files) | Duration: 23.5s
Files/second: 6.77 | Duration: 2.95s

~9.8x throughput | | **Total Test Suite** | **149.25s** | **9.78s** | **~15x faster overall** | ## Usage Example ```go // Clone with batch size of 100 blobs per request result, err := client.Clone(ctx, nanogit.CloneOptions{ Path: "/tmp/repo", Hash: commitHash, BatchSize: 100, // Fetch 100 blobs per request IncludePaths: []string{"src/**"}, // Works with path filtering }) ``` ## Testing - ✅ 7 new integration tests covering batch fetching scenarios - ✅ All existing tests pass (no regression) - ✅ Backward compatible (default behavior unchanged) - ✅ Works seamlessly with path filtering ## Implementation Notes The implementation follows the same pattern as tree batching in `tree.go`: - Processes entries in batches of specified size - Tracks missing blobs and retries individually - Maintains full backward compatibility with `BatchSize = 0` or `1` 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

body:
When one VPN fails in redundant mode, the system spams connectivity checks (~100/min), attempts API calls immediately after restart (causing failures), shows contradictory log messages about provisioning, and prematurely deletes newly-provisioned engines.

## Changes

**Throttle connectivity double-checks** (`gluetun.py`)
- Check engine connectivity once per 30s instead of continuously
- Prevents ~100 log messages → ~3 messages during VPN downtime

**Add restart grace period** (`gluetun.py`)
- Wait 15s after VPN restart before Gluetun API calls
- Applied to `get_forwarded_port()`, `get_forwarded_port_sync()`, `get_vpn_public_ip()`

**Centralize VPN recovery logic** (`health_manager.py`)
- New `_should_wait_for_vpn_recovery()` checks once per loop
- Skip both provisioning and replacement when waiting for VPN recovery
- Eliminates contradictory "won't provision... ensuring minimum" messages

**Add recovery stabilization period** (`monitor.py`, `gluetun.py`)
- Track `_last_recovery_time` per VPN
- Skip engine cleanup for 120s after recovery and during VPN degraded mode
- Prevents immediate deletion of newly-provisioned engines

**Test coverage** (`test_vpn_recovery_fixes.py`)
- Validates throttling, grace periods, recovery logic, cleanup skip
- 5/5 tests pass

## Example

Before:
```
18:16:55 VPN double-check: None of 5 engine(s) have internet connectivity
18:16:55 VPN double-check: None of 5 engine(s) have internet connectivity
18:16:55 VPN double-check: None of 5 engine(s) have internet connectivity
...100+ more...
18:18:09 Failed to get forwarded port: Connection refused
18:18:14 Starting 5 new engines
18:18:52 Cleaning up empty engine (just provisioned!)
```

After:
```
18:16:55 VPN double-check: None of 5 engine(s) have internet connectivity
[30s silence]
18:17:25 VPN double-check: None of 5 engine(s) have internet connectivity
[VPN restarts, waits 15s]
18:18:14 Starting 5 new engines
[Waits 120s before cleanup]
```

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->

> check the logs in vpn_exit.log, the flow is still not good when one of the vpns goes down. As soon as the engine goes down (in this case it is because it is exited but it should be the same when it's unhealthy) the system spam checks if engines have connectivity way too much and it fails to get its public ip (this shouldn't be done until a healthy state is recovered). Then this two contradictory messages show, the second one seems that the system is not taking into account that it should only run with limited engines (the ones from the other vpn): orchestrator  | 2025-11-07T17:17:54.792777147Z 2025-11-07 18:17:54,789 INFO app.services.health_manager: VPN 'gluetun' is unhealthy with 5 engines. Not provisioning new engines - waiting for VPN recovery. Running with 5/10 engines.
> orchestrator  | 2025-11-07T17:17:54.792799242Z 2025-11-07 18:17:54,789 INFO app.services.health_manager: Not enough healthy engines (5) to replace unhealthy ones. Ensuring minimum first. The engines should have already been brought down until either gluetun becomes healthy again or gets force restarted. Then after restarting it it doesn't wait enough till its healthy and can get a forwarded port from it. And then for some reason replacement engines are deleted and reprovisioned again. Which is a waste of resources.

# Implement 8 Authentication Security Improvements

## Summary

This PR implements 8 comprehensive security improvements to the authentication system, migrating from deprecated OAuth2 Password Grant to Authorization Code Flow with PKCE, and adding multiple layers of security protection.

**Key Changes:**
1. ✅ **Authorization Code Flow with PKCE** - Replaced deprecated Password Grant with modern PKCE flow
2. ✅ **Refresh Token Rotation** - Added `offline_access` scope and token expiration detection
3. ✅ **Rate Limiting** - Added Redis-based rate limiting to API Gateway (10-20 req/s per endpoint)
4. ✅ **MFA for Critical Operations** - Filter checks JWT `acr` claim for MFA on high-value operations
5. ✅ **Secrets Management** - Migrated hardcoded secrets to environment variables
6. ✅ **Audit Logging** - New AuditLog entity/service tracking authentication events
7. ✅ **Token Introspection** - Validates tokens with Keycloak for critical operations
8. ✅ **RBAC** - 9 role-based authorization rules with Keycloak role extraction

**Files Changed:**
- **API Gateway**: SecurityConfig (RBAC rules), 4 new filters, RateLimiterConfig, KeycloakRoleConverter, application.yml (rate limits + OAuth2 config)
- **User Service**: AuditLog entity/repo/service, UserServiceImpl (audit logging), application.yml (secrets)
- **Documentation**: KEYCLOAK_SETUP.md, SECRETS_MANAGEMENT.md, .env.example
- **Postman Collection**: Updated to Authorization Code Flow with PKCE

**All 7 services compile successfully.**

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

⚠️ **CRITICAL**: This PR has breaking changes and requires manual configuration steps before it will work.

- [ ] **Keycloak Configuration** - Follow `docs/KEYCLOAK_SETUP.md` to configure:
  - Enable PKCE (S256) and disable Direct Access Grants
  - Create roles: ADMIN, USER, SYSTEM
  - Configure MFA (OTP)
  - Set token lifespans and refresh token rotation
  - Verify role mapper includes `realm_access.roles` in JWT
  
- [ ] **Database Migration** - Create and run migration for `audit_logs` table in `user_service` database:
  ```sql
  CREATE TABLE audit_logs (
    id BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    user_id BIGINT,
    auth_id VARCHAR(255),
    event_type VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    ip_address VARCHAR(255),
    user_agent VARCHAR(255),
    details VARCHAR(1000),
    success BOOLEAN,
    created_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
  );
  ```

- [ ] **Redis Setup** - Install and start Redis for rate limiting, or verify in-memory fallback works:
  ```bash
  docker run -d -p 6379:6379 redis:latest
  ```

- [ ] **Environment Variables** - Set required secrets before starting services:
  ```bash
  export KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_SECRET=<your_gateway_secret>
  export KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_SECRET_API=<your_user_service_secret>
  ```

- [ ] **End-to-End Testing** - Test complete authentication flow:
  1. Start all services (Service Registry → Keycloak → API Gateway → User/Account/FundTransfer services)
  2. Register new user via POST `/api/users/register`
  3. Obtain token via Authorization Code Flow (use Postman collection)
  4. Verify role-based access (USER can access accounts, ADMIN can list all users)
  5. Test MFA requirement on fund transfer POST (should require `acr` claim with `mfa`)
  6. Verify audit logs in database for registration and status changes
  7. Test rate limiting by making >20 requests rapidly
  8. Verify token introspection works for critical operations

### Notes

**Potential Issues:**
- **RefreshTokenFilter** is incomplete - only detects expiring tokens but doesn't refresh them automatically
- **TokenIntrospectionFilter** adds latency due to HTTP calls to Keycloak on every critical operation
- **Breaking Change**: Existing clients using Password Grant (`password_credentials`) will stop working
- **Redis Required**: Rate limiting will fail if Redis is not running (no in-memory fallback implemented)

author: bubulalabu
body:
# Batched Table Functions with LATERAL Join Support

**Note: This is a draft PR for gathering feedback on the approach. It's working, but not polished yet**

I'm interested to hear opinions if this is the right path forward before starting to finalize the PR

## Which issue does this PR close?

Closes #18121.

---

## The Problem

DataFusion's current table function API (`TableFunctionImpl`) requires constant arguments at planning time and returns a `TableProvider`. This prevents LATERAL joins where table functions need to correlate with outer query rows.

```sql
-- Current limitation: Cannot do this
SELECT * FROM metrics m
CROSS JOIN LATERAL generate_series(m.start_time, m.end_time) AS t(ts);
```

### Current Architecture Limitations

```rust
// Current API
trait TableFunctionImpl {
    fn call(&self, args: &[Expr]) -> Result<Arc<dyn TableProvider>>;
}
```

**Problems**:
- Planning-time evaluation: Arguments must be constants, can't reference table columns
- No LATERAL support: Can't correlate function calls with input rows
- Separate TableProvider per call: Inefficient for batch processing

---

## Proposed Solution

Introduce a new trait that processes arrays of arguments (batched invocation) and returns output with input row mapping for correlation:

```rust
#[async_trait]
trait BatchedTableFunctionImpl {
    async fn invoke_batch(
        &self,
        args: &[ArrayRef],            // Already-evaluated arrays
        projection: Option<&[usize]>, 
        filters: &[Expr],
        limit: Option<usize>,
    ) -> Result<BatchResultStream>;
}

// Results map back to input rows for LATERAL
struct BatchResultChunk {
    output: RecordBatch,
    input_row_indices: Vec<u32>,  // contain the indexes that correspond to the input indexes for every output row 
}
```

### Key Design Decisions

**1. Arrays as Arguments**
- Like `ScalarUDF` - receives evaluated data, not planning-time expressions
- Enables batched processing: process multiple function calls in one `invoke_batch`
- Natural fit for LATERAL: array elements correspond to input rows

**2. Async API**
- Matches `TableProvider::scan()` async pattern

**3. Direct Pushdown Parameters**
- Matches `TableProvider::scan()` pattern
- Function gets projection/filter/limit directly in `invoke_batch()`

**3. Streaming Results**
- Returns `Stream<BatchResultChunk>` for memory-bounded execution
- Chunks include `input_row_indices` for efficient LATERAL join implementation

---

## Architecture Overview

### Execution Flow Example: generate_series(start, end)

**Input batch**:
```
┌────┬───────┬─────┐
│ id │ start │ end │
├────┼───────┼─────┤
│ 1  │ 10    │ 12  │
│ 2  │ 20    │ 22  │
└────┴───────┴─────┘
```

**Evaluate args** → `start=[10, 20]`, `end=[12, 22]`

**invoke_batch** → Stream of chunks:
```rust
Chunk {
    output: [10, 11, 12],     // generated values for start=[10] and end=[12] 
    input_row_indices: [0, 0, 0]  // all from input row 0
}
Chunk {
    output: [20, 21, 22],
    input_row_indices: [1, 1, 1]  // all from input row 1
}
```

**Combine** using indices → Final output:
```
┌────┬───────┬─────┬───────┐
│ id │ start │ end │ value │
├────┼───────┼─────┼───────┤
│ 1  │ 10    │ 12  │ 10    │
│ 1  │ 10    │ 12  │ 11    │
│ 1  │ 10    │ 12  │ 12    │
│ 2  │ 20    │ 22  │ 20    │
│ 2  │ 20    │ 22  │ 21    │
│ 2  │ 20    │ 22  │ 22    │
└────┴───────┴─────┴───────┘
```

---

## What's Included

### Core Components

**1. New Trait** (`datafusion/catalog/src/table.rs`)
```rust
pub trait BatchedTableFunctionImpl: Send + Sync + Debug {
    fn name(&self) -> &str;
    fn signature(&self) -> &Signature;
    fn return_type(&self, arg_types: &[DataType]) -> Result<Schema>;

    async fn invoke_batch(
        &self,
        args: &[ArrayRef],
        projection: Option<&[usize]>,
        filters: &[Expr],
        limit: Option<usize>,
    ) -> Result<BatchResultStream>;
}
```

**2. Logical Plan Nodes** (`datafusion/expr/src/logical_plan/plan.rs`)
- `StandaloneBatchedTableFunction` - for `SELECT * FROM func(1, 100)`
- `LateralBatchedTableFunction` - for `SELECT * FROM t LATERAL func(t.x)`

**3. Physical Executor** (`datafusion/catalog/src/batched_function/exec.rs`)
- Unified `BatchedTableFunctionExec` with two modes (Standalone/Lateral)
- Handles argument evaluation, function invocation, and result combination

**6. Optimizer Rules** (`datafusion/optimizer/src/`)
- Extended projection/filter/limit pushdown to new logical plan nodes

**7. Reference Implementation** (`datafusion/functions-table/src/generate_series_batched.rs`)
- Complete example showing the implementation pattern
- Demonstrates limit pushdown optimization

### SQL Examples Enabled

```sql
-- Standalone: constant arguments
SELECT * FROM generate_series(1, 100);

-- LATERAL: correlate with outer table
SELECT m.metric_id, t.ts
FROM metrics m
CROSS JOIN LATERAL generate_series(m.start_time, m.end_time) AS t(ts);

-- With optimizations (limit pushdown)
SELECT * FROM generate_series(1, 1000000) LIMIT 10;
-- Only generates ~10 rows instead of 1M
```

---

## Testing

**Comprehensive test coverage**:
- Unit tests in `batched_function/exec.rs`
- Integration tests in `core/tests/batched_table_function.rs`
- SQL logic tests in `sqllogictest/test_files/lateral.slt`
- All tests pass

---

## Open Questions

### 1. Is a new trait the right approach?

This PR introduces `BatchedTableFunctionImpl` as a separate trait. An alternative would be to use `TableProvider` wrappers.

### 2. Is the API appropriate?

```rust
async fn invoke_batch(
    args: &[ArrayRef],
    projection: Option<&[usize]>,
    filters: &[Expr],
    limit: Option<usize>,
) -> Result<BatchResultStream>;
```

### 3. Is "Batched" the right terminology?

Current naming: `BatchedTableFunctionImpl`, `StandaloneBatchedTableFunction`, etc.

### 4. Should we keep both APIs or eventually deprecate `TableFunctionImpl`?

---

## User-Facing Changes

**New SQL capabilities**:
```sql
-- LATERAL joins
SELECT t.id, s.value
FROM my_table t
CROSS JOIN LATERAL generate_series(t.start, t.end) AS s(value);
```

**New API for function developers**:
```rust
// Implement the trait
struct MyFunction { /* ... */ }

#[async_trait]
impl BatchedTableFunctionImpl for MyFunction {
    async fn invoke_batch(/* ... */) -> Result<BatchResultStream> {
        // Your implementation
    }
}

// Register in session
ctx.state_ref()
    .write()
    .register_batched_table_function("my_func", Arc::new(MyFunction));
```

**Breaking changes**: 

The PR adds two new values to the LogicalPlan enum.

# Fix: Gateway Test Suite Isolation and Middleware Improvements

## 🎫 Tickets
- Related: GATE-001 through GATE-013 (Gateway component development)

## 🎯 Purpose
Resolve critical test isolation issues discovered when running the full test suite. Two OAuth documentation tests were failing in the full suite but passing when run individually, indicating module caching and configuration isolation problems. Additionally, improve middleware consistency and error handling.

**Context:**
While developing the gateway component (GATE-001 through GATE-013), running the full test suite revealed test isolation issues:
- OAuth documentation tests failed in full suite (passed individually)
- Prometheus metrics registration conflicts when reloading modules
- Security tests needed proper validation configuration isolation

## 📝 Changes

### Fixed
- **Test Isolation**: OAuth documentation tests now pass in full suite (2/2 failures resolved)
- **Metrics Labels**: Standardized Prometheus label names from "endpoint" to "path"
- **Validation Errors**: Improved error messages and response handling in validation middleware
- **Security Test Configuration**: Proper isolation for security tests with validation enabled

### Added
- Module-scoped monkeypatch fixture for OAuth test configuration
- Security-specific conftest.py for proper test isolation
- Comprehensive header skip list for validation middleware
- secure_client fixture for security integration tests

### Changed
- OAuth tests use monkeypatch instead of module reloading
- Validation middleware returns JSONResponse instead of raising exceptions
- Security audit tests check default settings instead of runtime overrides
- Test configuration uses `setdefault` for better isolation

## 🔧 Technical Details

### Approach:
**Problem**: Gateway modules were imported by earlier tests with default settings (OAuth disabled), creating a cached settings singleton before OAuth documentation tests could set their environment variables.

**Initial Attempt**: Module reloading - caused Prometheus metrics registration conflicts.

**Final Solution**: Use pytest's monkeypatch to modify settings object directly, avoiding module reload issues.

### Key Files:
- `src/gateway/main.py` - Added missing OpenAPI metadata fields
- `src/gateway/middleware/metrics.py` - Standardized label names
- `src/gateway/middleware/validation.py` - Improved error handling and header skip list
- `tests/gateway/test_openapi_documentation.py` - Fixed OAuth test isolation with monkeypatch
- `tests/gateway/security/conftest.py` - New security test configuration
- `tests/gateway/conftest.py` - Improved test isolation with setdefault
- `tests/gateway/security/test_security_audit.py` - Fixed validation setting checks
- `tests/gateway/security/test_security_integration.py` - Use shared secure_client fixture
- `tests/gateway/test_middleware.py` - Updated metrics label assertions

### Implementation Details:

**OAuth Test Isolation:**
```python
@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def client(monkeypatch_module) -> TestClient:
    from gateway.config import settings

    monkeypatch_module.setattr(settings, "OAUTH_ENABLED", True)
    monkeypatch_module.setattr(settings, "REALTIME_ENABLED", True)

    from gateway.auth.oauth.registry import initialize_oauth_providers
    initialize_oauth_providers()

    from gateway.main import create_app
    return TestClient(create_app())
```

**Security Test Isolation:**
```python
def pytest_configure(config):
    os.environ["GATEWAY_VALIDATION_ENABLED"] = "true"
    # Clear cached modules and Prometheus registry
```

**Validation Middleware Improvements:**
- Added content-type, accept, trace IDs to header skip list
- Changed error messages to avoid revealing attack detection details
- Return JSONResponse instead of raising HTTPException for proper middleware flow

## 🧪 Testing

**Test Coverage:**
- [x] All OAuth documentation tests pass in full suite (18/18)
- [x] All security integration tests pass with validation enabled
- [x] Full gateway test suite passes (483/483 tests)
- [x] Metrics middleware tests updated for new label names
- [x] No Prometheus registration conflicts

**Before Fix:**
- Full test suite: 2 failed, 5632 passed
- OAuth tests: Failed in full suite, passed individually
- Issue: Test isolation problem

**After Fix:**
- Full test suite: 0 failed, 5634 passed
- OAuth tests: Pass in both isolation and full suite
- All 483 gateway tests passing

**Test Scenarios:**
1. ✅ OAuth documentation tests run individually
2. ✅ OAuth documentation tests in full gateway suite
3. ✅ OAuth documentation tests in complete test suite
4. ✅ Security tests with validation enabled
5. ✅ No Prometheus metric conflicts between test modules

## 📊 Impact

**Performance:**
- No performance impact
- Improved test suite reliability
- Faster test debugging (no false positives from isolation issues)

**Breaking Changes:**
- [ ] No breaking changes
- Metrics label change is internal only (middleware implementation)

**Migration Required:**
- [ ] No migration needed

## 🔗 References
- Branch: feature/gate-component
- Related tickets: GATE-001 through GATE-013
- Test suite log: `.docs/FULL_TEST_SUITE_RUN_LOG.log`

## ✅ Checklist
- [x] Code follows project style guidelines
- [x] All tests pass locally (5634/5634)
- [x] Documentation updated (PR description, commit messages)
- [x] No console errors/warnings
- [x] Reviewed own code
- [x] Test isolation issues resolved
- [x] Ready for review

## 📋 Review Notes

**Focus Areas:**
1. **Test isolation approach**: Verify monkeypatch is the right solution vs alternatives
2. **Security test configuration**: Ensure validation is properly enabled for security tests
3. **Middleware changes**: Review error handling and header skip list additions
4. **Metrics label change**: Confirm "path" is more standard than "endpoint"

**Testing Recommendations:**
- Run full test suite to verify no regressions
- Run gateway tests in isolation to verify they still pass
- Check Prometheus metrics output to ensure labels are correct

---

- `3fff688` fix(gateway/middleware): standardize metrics labels and improve validation
- `0781f9f` test(gateway): fix test isolation for OAuth and security tests

author: missingroberto
body: ## What this PR does / why we need it Fixes a bug where the DELETE endpoint `/repositories/{name}/files/{path}` does not include the `ref` field in its `ResourceWrapper` response when deleting files to a branch, even though the ref is sent as a required query parameter. This causes the branch workflow success handler to fail silently in the frontend. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Open a git provisioned dashboard 2. Go to settings page → scroll to bottom → delete button 3. Push changes to a branch 4. Submit the changes 5. Observe the API response - ref field is missing ## Root Cause The issue was an inverted boolean condition in the `Delete` method in `dualwriter.go`. The code was setting `file.Ref = opts.Ref` when `shouldUpdateGrafanaDB` returned true (main branch operations), but it should have been setting it when false (branch operations), since we read the file with an empty ref. ## The Fix Changed line 103 from: \`\`\`go if r.shouldUpdateGrafanaDB(opts, nil) { \`\`\` to: \`\`\`go if !r.shouldUpdateGrafanaDB(opts, nil) { \`\`\` This ensures the ref field is properly included in the ResourceWrapper response for branch operations, matching the behavior of folder deletes and other operations. ## Which issue(s) this PR fixes Fix https://github.com/grafana/git-ui-sync-project/issues/639

author: kapral18
body:
## Summary

Suppresses `console.error` warnings from jsdom when parsing CSS `@container` queries in Jest tests.

## Problem

When running Jest tests with components that use EUI's responsive container queries (e.g., `EuiPageHeader`), jsdom 20.0.1 fails to parse `@container` syntax and floods the console with errors:

```
console.error
  There was a problem inserting the following rule: "@container (max-width: 768px){.css-13dn9dx-euiPageHeaderContent__leftSideItems{min-inline-size:50%;}}" Error: Unexpected } (line 1, char 101)
    at parseError (node_modules/cssom/lib/parse.js:62:15)
    at Object.parse (node_modules/cssom/lib/parse.js:385:7)
    at CSSStyleSheet.CSSOM.CSSStyleSheet.insertRule (node_modules/cssom/lib/CSSStyleSheet.js:43:22)
    at StyleSheet.insert (node_modules/@emotion/sheet/dist/emotion-sheet.cjs.dev.js:129:15)
```

This warning appears 4 times per test render, polluting test output and making it harder to spot real issues.

## Root Cause

- **jsdom 20.0.1** (Oct 2022) uses **cssom 0.5.0** which doesn't support `@container` queries
- EUI components use `@container` for progressive responsive design via Emotion
- When Emotion tries to insert these rules, cssom fails to parse them and logs errors

## Solution

Added `console.error` suppression in `emotion.js` test setup for `@container`-related parsing errors.

## Why This Is Safe

1. **Not a real error** - Just a jsdom/cssom limitation, not a test failure
2. **Doesn't affect test functionality** - Container queries are progressive enhancement; tests verify logic, not responsive behavior  
3. **Established pattern** - The file already suppresses similar CSS parsing warnings
4. **Temporary** - Can be removed after upgrading jsdom to 24.1.0+

## Future Work

- **Short term** (this PR): Suppress warnings ✅
- **Medium term**: Upgrade jsdom from 20.0.1 to 24.1.0+ (May 2024) to eliminate parse errors
- **Long term**: Full `@container` evaluation support (jsdom#3858 remains open, but not needed for tests)

## References

- https://github.com/jsdom/jsdom/issues/3597 - Parsing errors (fixed in jsdom 24.1.0+)
- https://github.com/jsdom/jsdom/issues/3858 - Evaluation support (still open, but acceptable)

## Test Plan

1. Run any Jest test that renders EUI components with container queries
2. Verify no console warnings appear
3. Verify tests still pass

Free previously allocated `quantize_index` and `quantize_sort` arrays before reallocating them. This prevents memory leaks when `png_set_quantize()` is called multiple times on the same `png_struct`.

body:
# Translation Coordinator Contract

## Overview

This PR introduces the `translation-coordinator` smart contract for the Medical Translation Services platform, a blockchain-based healthcare communication system that connects certified medical interpreters with healthcare providers and patients requiring language assistance.

## Contract Description

The translation-coordinator contract provides a comprehensive solution for managing medical interpretation services on the Stacks blockchain. It handles interpreter registration, credential verification, service request management, session tracking, and quality assurance through a rating system.

## Key Features

### Interpreter Management
- **Registration System**: Interpreters can register with their language proficiencies, credentials, and hourly rates
- **Credential Verification**: Contract owner can verify interpreter qualifications before they can accept assignments
- **Language Certifications**: Support for multiple language certifications with proficiency levels and expiration dates
- **Availability Tracking**: Real-time tracking of interpreter availability status

### Service Request Workflow
- **Request Creation**: Healthcare providers can create service requests with specific language requirements
- **Interpreter Assignment**: Matching of available, verified interpreters to service requests
- **Session Management**: Complete lifecycle tracking from session start to completion
- **Duration Tracking**: Automatic calculation of actual session duration

### Quality Assurance
- **Multi-dimensional Rating System**: Rate interpreters on accuracy, professionalism, and timeliness
- **Feedback Collection**: Capture detailed feedback for each completed session
- **Average Rating Calculation**: Automatic updating of interpreter ratings based on service history
- **Session Notes**: Support for detailed session documentation

### Analytics & Tracking
- **Provider Statistics**: Track total requests, sessions, duration, and spending per healthcare provider
- **Language Usage**: Monitor which languages are being requested most frequently
- **Service History**: Complete audit trail of all interpretation services

## Technical Implementation

### Data Structures

**Interpreters Map**: Stores comprehensive interpreter profiles including:
- Owner principal
- Primary and secondary languages
- Credentials and certification date
- Status (pending, verified, active, suspended)
- Total sessions completed
- Average rating
- Availability flag
- Hourly rate

**Service Requests Map**: Manages interpretation service requests with:
- Requester principal
- Required language
- Requested duration
- Urgency level (1-5)
- Assigned interpreter
- Request status
- Special requirements

**Interpretation Sessions Map**: Tracks active and completed sessions:
- Request and interpreter IDs
- Provider principal
- Start and end times
- Actual duration
- Session status
- Language used
- Session notes

**Session Ratings Map**: Captures service quality metrics:
- Overall rating (1-5)
- Accuracy, professionalism, and timeliness scores
- Detailed feedback text
- Rating timestamp

**Language Certifications Map**: Validates interpreter credentials:
- Proficiency level (1-5)
- Certification status
- Certifying organization
- Expiration date

**Usage Statistics Map**: Aggregates provider service data:
- Total requests and sessions
- Total duration and spending
- Languages utilized

### Core Functions

#### Public Functions (15 total)
1. `register-interpreter` - Register new interpreters with credentials
2. `verify-interpreter` - Owner-only credential verification
3. `add-language-certification` - Add language certifications for interpreters
4. `create-service-request` - Create new interpretation service requests
5. `assign-interpreter` - Match interpreters to service requests
6. `start-session` - Begin an interpretation session
7. `complete-session` - Mark session as completed with notes
8. `rate-session` - Rate completed sessions with multi-dimensional scoring
9. `update-availability` - Toggle interpreter availability
10. `update-platform-fee` - Owner-only fee adjustment
11. `update-provider-statistics` - Track provider usage metrics

#### Read-Only Functions (11 total)
- Getters for interpreters, service requests, sessions, and ratings
- Statistical queries (totals, availability checks, rating lookups)
- Provider usage statistics retrieval

### Security Features

- **Access Control**: Functions restricted by role (owner, interpreter, provider)
- **Authorization Checks**: Verify caller identity before state modifications
- **Status Validation**: Ensure interpreters are verified before accepting assignments
- **Rating Bounds**: Enforce 1-5 rating scale across all metrics
- **Session State Management**: Prevent invalid state transitions

### Error Handling

The contract defines comprehensive error codes:
- `err-owner-only` (u100) - Unauthorized owner-only operation
- `err-not-found` (u101) - Resource not found
- `err-already-exists` (u102) - Duplicate resource
- `err-unauthorized` (u103) - Insufficient permissions
- `err-invalid-rating` (u104) - Rating out of bounds
- `err-session-active` (u105) - Session already active
- `err-session-not-active` (u106) - Session not in progress
- `err-invalid-duration` (u107) - Invalid duration specified
- `err-interpreter-unavailable` (u108) - Interpreter not available
- `err-invalid-credentials` (u109) - Invalid credential data

## Contract Statistics

- **Total Lines**: 479 lines
- **Constants**: 17
- **Data Variables**: 4
- **Data Maps**: 6
- **Public Functions**: 11
- **Read-Only Functions**: 11
- **Error Codes**: 10

## Testing Considerations

The contract should be tested for:
- Interpreter registration and verification workflows
- Service request creation and assignment
- Session lifecycle (start, complete, rate)

# Problem
The FX backend currently allocates tensors on an exact device index, such as `"cuda:0"`. In contrast, the Python backend allocates on a device type, such as `"cuda"`. This avoids edge cases where fake tensor propagation can fail due to mismatched devices.

# Fix
Allocate tensors on `device.type` instead of the device.

# Test plan
Added a CI test passing in sample inputs on an indexed device, and checking that the output device in the generated FX graph is not indexed.

## Summary  
Final fix for Jinja2 whitespace issues - GitLab CI YAML generation.

## Problem
GitLab CI validation failing with:
```
YAMLException: bad indentation of a mapping entry (15:27)
  TF_CLI_ARGS: "-no-color".terraform_base_vpc:
```

## Root Cause
`{%- for` was removing newlines after YAML blocks, causing invalid syntax.

## Solution
Changed all loop markers to preserve newlines:
- `{%- for` → `{% for` (start of loop)
- `{%- endfor` → `{% endfor` (end of loop)
- Keep `-%}` to trim trailing spaces where needed

## Testing
Generated YAML will now be valid and pass gitlab-ci-local validation.

<!-- Thanks for contributing to Artemis! Before you submit your pull request, please make sure to check all tasks by putting an x in the [ ] (don't: [x ], [ x], do: [x]). Remove not applicable tasks and do not leave them unchecked -->
<!-- If your pull request is not ready for review yet, create a draft pull request! -->

### Checklist
#### General
- [x] I tested **all** changes and their related features with **all** corresponding user types on a test server.
- [x] I chose a title conforming to the [naming conventions for pull requests](https://docs.artemis.cit.tum.de/dev/development-process/development-process.html#naming-conventions-for-github-pull-requests).
- [x] Language: I followed the [guidelines for inclusive, diversity-sensitive, and appreciative language](https://docs.artemis.cit.tum.de/dev/guidelines/language-guidelines/).

#### Server
- [x] **Important**: I implemented the changes with a [very good performance](https://docs.artemis.cit.tum.de/dev/guidelines/performance/) and prevented too many (unnecessary) and too complex database calls.
- [x] I **strictly** followed the [server coding and design guidelines](https://docs.artemis.cit.tum.de/dev/guidelines/server/).
- [x] I added multiple integration tests (Spring) related to the features (with a high test coverage).
- [x] I documented the Java code using JavaDoc style.

#### Client
- [x] I **strictly** followed the [client coding and design guidelines](https://docs.artemis.cit.tum.de/dev/guidelines/client/).
- [x] I added multiple integration tests (Jest) related to the features (with a high test coverage), while following the [test guidelines](https://docs.artemis.cit.tum.de/dev/guidelines/client-tests/).
- [x] I translated all newly inserted strings into English and German.

#### Changes affecting Programming Exercises
- [x] **High priority**: I tested **all** changes and their related features with **all** corresponding user types on a test server configured with the **integrated lifecycle setup** (LocalVC and LocalCI).

### Motivation and Context
On LocalCI, build containers for programming exercises previously only supported toggling network access on or off. 
As instructors need the option to use a custom Docker network, this PR removes the old network toggle and replaces it with a custom docker network selector.
The custom network might be needed when running truly private tests: We still want the container to be able to connect to the Maven dependency cache or a database server the tests run against, but _not_ to any other locations.
Closes https://github.com/ls1intum/Artemis/issues/10431.

### Description
Implements the custom Docker network selector end-to-end across LocalCI, the build agent, and the instructor UI:

- `DockerRunConfig` now stores the requested network name instead of a boolean. Build job execution configures the desired network directly on the container `HostConfig`, and LocalCI validates that the value is part of the `allowed-custom-networks` list before queuing a build.
- LocalCI exposes that allow-list via the profile info endpoint, enabling the build configuration form to replace the old “disable network access” checkbox with a dropdown (Default / None / configured networks). The warning banner is now only shown when the `none` option is selected, and the choice is serialized together with the other Docker flags.
- Documentation and defaults describe the new `allowed-custom-networks` property, while integration and component tests cover network serialization, accepted names, and the failure mode for invalid networks.

### Steps for Testing
Please create a docker network and start a simple whoami server using these commands:
```
docker network create artemis-ci-network
docker run -d --rm --name whoami --hostname whoami-hostname --network artemis-ci-network traefik/whoami
```

Add this to `application-local.yml`:
```
artemis:
    continuous-integration:
        container-flags-limit:
            allowed-custom-networks: none, artemis-ci-network
```

Create a new course and create a new programming exercise. 
Enable `Customize Build Configuration` and confirm the custom network is set to `Default (Bridge)`.
Observe, that the options `Default (Bridge)`, `None` and `artemis-ci-network` are available.

Edit the Programming Exercise `Test Repository`. Delete the existing tests.
Then add the following test into the file `test/test/NetworkReachabilityTest.java`:
```
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertTrue;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.io.BufferedReader;
import java.io.InputStreamReader;
import java.net.HttpURLConnection;
import java.net.URL;

class NetworkReachabilityTest {

    String requestAndReturnBody(String urlString) throws IOException {
        URL url = new URL(urlString);
        HttpURLConnection conn = (HttpURLConnection) url.openConnection();
        conn.setConnectTimeout(3000);
        conn.setReadTimeout(3000);
        conn.connect();

        int code = conn.getResponseCode();
        BufferedReader br = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(conn.getInputStream()));
        String body = br.readLine();
        br.close();

        if (code == 200) return body;
        else return null;
    }

    @Test
    void canReachServiceOnCustomNetwork() throws IOException {
        String body = requestAndReturnBody("http://whoami/");
        assertTrue(body != null && body.contains("whoami-hostname"), "Expected 200 from http-svc on custom network");
    }

    @Test
    void canReachServiceOnTheInternet() throws IOException {
        String body = requestAndReturnBody("https://www.google.com/");
        assertTrue(body != null && body.contains("<title>Google</title>"), "Expected 200 from google on bridge network");
    }
}
```

Navigate to the Information page for the Programming Exercise, scroll to `Solution Result` and resubmit it.
Observe, how the `canReachServiceOnCustomNetwork` test fails and the `canReachServiceOnTheInternet` test succeeds.

Now change the custom network to `None`.
Navigate to the Information page for the Programming Exercise, scroll to `Solution Result` and resubmit it.
Observe, how the build fails as it cannot fetch the required dependencies.

Now change the custom network to `artemis-ci-network`. This was created as a bridge network, so the build should succeed.
Navigate to the Information page for the Programming Exercise, scroll to `Solution Result` and resubmit it.
Observe, how the `canReachServiceOnCustomNetwork` test succeeds and the `canReachServiceOnTheInternet` test succeeds.


#### Exam Mode Testing
There is no logic specific to exam mode.

body:
## Overview

This pull request introduces a comprehensive blockchain-based parking violation management system built with Clarity smart contracts on the Stacks blockchain. The system provides municipalities with transparent, immutable, and efficient tools for managing the complete lifecycle of parking enforcement operations.

## Key Features

### Citation Management
- **Issue Citations**: Enforcement officers can issue parking violations with complete details including license plate, offense description, fine amount, location, and due date
- **Citation Tracking**: All citations are stored immutably on-chain with unique IDs and comprehensive metadata
- **Status Management**: Citations progress through various states (active, paid, appealed, dismissed, overdue) with proper validation

### Payment Processing
- **Payment Recording**: Secure on-chain payment tracking with support for multiple payment methods
- **Partial Payments**: System supports partial payments with automatic balance calculation
- **Payment History**: Complete audit trail of all payment transactions including payer, amount, method, and timestamp
- **Real-time Balance Updates**: Vehicle history automatically updates with each payment

### Appeals System
- **Appeal Submission**: Vehicle owners can submit appeals with detailed reasoning and evidence URLs
- **Review Workflow**: Appeals officers can review, approve, or deny appeals with decision notes
- **One Appeal Per Citation**: Built-in validation prevents duplicate appeals for the same citation
- **Citation Status Updates**: Approved appeals automatically dismiss citations; denied appeals restore active status

### Vehicle Boot Coordination
- **Boot Placement**: Enforcement officers can place boots on vehicles with repeat violations
- **Multi-Citation Tracking**: Boot records can reference up to 10 associated citations
- **Boot Removal**: Controlled boot removal process with timestamp recording
- **Boot Status Tracking**: Real-time tracking of active boot placements

### Vehicle History
- **Aggregated Data**: Complete violation history per license plate
- **Financial Summary**: Total citations, fines, payments, and outstanding balances
- **Active Citation List**: Track up to 20 active citations per vehicle
- **Boot Status**: Current boot placement status per vehicle

## Technical Implementation

### Smart Contract Architecture

**Data Structures:**
- Citations map: Stores all parking violation records
- Payments map: Records all payment transactions
- Appeals map: Manages appeal submissions and reviews
- Boots map: Tracks boot placement and removal
- Vehicle-history map: Aggregates data per license plate
- Citation-appeals map: Links citations to their appeals

**Authorization System:**
- Role-based access control (enforcement officers, payment processors, appeals officers)
- Contract owner has administrative privileges
- Each role has specific function permissions

**Counter Variables:**
- Citation nonce: Sequential ID generation for citations
- Payment nonce: Unique payment transaction IDs
- Appeal nonce: Sequential appeal IDs
- Boot nonce: Sequential boot record IDs

### Core Functions

#### Public Functions

1. **add-enforcement-officer**: Authorize enforcement officers (owner only)
2. **add-payment-processor**: Authorize payment processors (owner only)
3. **add-appeals-officer**: Authorize appeals officers (owner only)
4. **issue-citation**: Create new parking violation citations
5. **process-payment**: Record payment transactions and update balances
6. **submit-appeal**: Allow vehicle owners to appeal citations
7. **review-appeal**: Enable appeals officers to review and decide appeals
8. **place-boot**: Coordinate vehicle boot placement
9. **remove-boot**: Record boot removal with timestamp

#### Read-Only Functions

1. **get-citation**: Retrieve citation details by ID
2. **get-payment**: Fetch payment transaction records
3. **get-appeal**: Access appeal information
4. **get-boot**: Query boot placement records
5. **get-vehicle-history**: View complete vehicle violation history
6. **get-citation-appeal**: Find appeal associated with a citation

### Security Features

- **Authorization Checks**: All sensitive operations require appropriate role permissions
- **Status Validation**: Prevents invalid state transitions (e.g., paying already-paid citations)
- **Amount Validation**: Ensures payment amounts don't exceed outstanding balances
- **Duplicate Prevention**: Blocks multiple appeals for the same citation
- **Boot Status Verification**: Validates boot placement and removal operations

### Data Integrity

- **Immutable Records**: All citations, payments, and appeals are permanently recorded
- **Automatic Updates**: Vehicle history updates automatically with each transaction
- **Balance Tracking**: Real-time calculation of outstanding balances
- **Timestamp Recording**: All operations include blockchain timestamp (stacks-block-height)

## Contract Specifications

- **Language**: Clarity (version compatible with Clarinet)
- **Lines of Code**: 448 lines
- **Contract Name**: violation-manager
- **Dependencies**: None (no external contract calls or traits)

## Testing

The contract includes:
- Comprehensive syntax validation (passes clarinet check)
- TypeScript test file scaffold in tests/violation-manager.test.ts
- Ready for unit test implementation

## Use Cases

1. **Municipal Parking Enforcement**: Cities can deploy this system for transparent, accountable parking violation management
2. **Private Parking Facilities**: Commercial parking operators can track violations and payments
3. **Campus Parking**: Universities and corporate campuses can manage internal parking enforcement
4. **Audit and Compliance**: Immutable blockchain records provide complete audit trails
5. **Dispute Resolution**: Structured appeals process with evidence submission

## Benefits

- **Transparency**: All operations recorded on public blockchain
- **Accountability**: Immutable records prevent tampering or fraud
- **Efficiency**: Automated status updates and balance calculations
- **Fairness**: Structured appeals process with evidence support
- **Auditability**: Complete transaction history for compliance and reporting

## Configuration

The contract uses the following configurable elements:

- Maximum 20 active citations per vehicle
- Maximum 10 citations per boot record
- String length limits: License plates (20 chars), locations (128 chars), descriptions (256 chars), reasons (512 chars)
- Error codes ranging from u100-u109 for various failure conditions

## Future Enhancements

Potential additions in future versions:
- Payment plan scheduling
- Automated fine escalation for overdue violations
- Integration with DMV databases
- Mobile notification triggers
- Multi-language support for notices
- Analytics and reporting functions

## Deployment Considerations

1. **Initial Setup**: Deploy contract and set contract owner
2. **Authorization**: Add enforcement officers, payment processors, and appeals officers
3. **Integration**: Connect to existing municipal systems via API layer
4. **Testing**: Conduct thorough testing on testnet before mainnet deployment
5. **Monitoring**: Implement monitoring for contract operations and events

## Conclusion

This smart contract provides a robust foundation for blockchain-based parking violation management. The system ensures transparency, accountability, and efficiency while maintaining the flexibility needed for real-world municipal operations. All code follows Clarity best practices and has been validated for syntax correctness.

author: mergify[bot]
body:
## Description

This closes https://github.com/ros2/rmw_zenoh/issues/852. rmw_zenoh failed to pass the test since the publisher declared in `test_async_sub` was accidentally detected by the subsequent `test_pub_sub` (the tests run in alphabetical order). The root cause is that the publisher node is not explicitly destroyed during the rclpy shutdown. 

To clarify, this behavior stems from the different mechanism used in rmw_zenoh compared to other DDS implementations. Specifically, the shutdown of rmw_zenoh doesn't immediately close the Zenoh session as long as other nodes are still alive. This aligns with the RMW philosophy that nodes and their associated entities such as publishers, subscriptions, and so on, are not explicitly destroyed by rmw_shutdown.

Introduing a sleep after `rclpy.shutdown` does not solve the issue because the node data remain referenced until the object destruction phase. Meanwhile, the next test begins immediately and reads the stale liveliness token, causing the test to fail.

This fix adotps the approach used in other tests by explicitly cleaning up the nodes to avoid such stale references.

author: mindhivefi
body:
## Summary

Implements OpenAPI 3.0 specification compliance for binary data handling in generated clients. Fixes runtime errors where APIs return base64-encoded strings for binary fields (per OpenAPI standard `format: "byte"`), but generated clients expected pre-decoded bytes objects.

### Changes

- **BaseSchema.from_dict()**: Automatically decodes base64 strings to bytes when field type is `bytes`
- **BaseSchema.to_dict()**: Automatically encodes bytes to base64 strings for API compatibility
- **Enhanced type extraction**: Handles both `typing.Union` and `types.UnionType` for Python 3.10+ union syntax (`bytes | None`)

### Impact

- **High Impact**: Fixes critical runtime errors in all generated clients with binary fields
- **Zero Breaking Changes**: Backward compatible, adds missing functionality
- **Standards Compliant**: Follows OpenAPI 3.0 and RFC 4648 base64 encoding

## Technical Details

### Implementation

**File**: `src/pyopenapi_gen/core/schemas.py`
- Added `base64` and `types` imports
- Enhanced `_extract_base_type()` for modern Python union syntax
- Added base64 decoding in `from_dict()` at line 74-75
- Added base64 encoding in `to_dict()` at line 110-111
- Total: 15 lines changed (12 additions, 3 modifications)

### Test Coverage

**File**: `tests/core/test_schemas.py`
- Added 22 comprehensive tests (279 lines)
- Coverage: Basic operations, optional fields, round-trip, edge cases
- Edge cases tested: Empty bytes, control chars, 1MB files, image headers, unicode

### Quality Assurance

✅ All 1,405 tests pass (100% success rate)
✅ Code coverage: 89.22% (above 85% requirement)
✅ 100% coverage on modified file (schemas.py: 80/80 statements)
✅ Linting: All checks passed (ruff, black)
✅ Type checking: mypy strict mode - 0 issues
✅ Security: Bandit scan clean
✅ Performance: Tested with 1MB files (<0.05s)

## Examples

### Before (Runtime Error)
```python
# API returns: {"content": "SGVsbG8sIFdvcmxkIQ=="}
doc = DocumentWithBinary.from_dict(data)
doc.content.decode('utf-8')  # ❌ AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'decode'
```

### After (Works Correctly)
```python
# API returns: {"content": "SGVsbG8sIFdvcmxkIQ=="}
doc = DocumentWithBinary.from_dict(data)
doc.content.decode('utf-8')  # ✅ Returns: "Hello, World!"
```

## Related Issues

Resolves runtime errors in downstream projects where OpenAPI specs define binary fields with `format: "byte"` (standard base64 encoding). This fix is required for the Mainio project and any other projects using binary data in generated clients.

author: mergify[bot]
body:
## Description

This closes https://github.com/ros2/rmw_zenoh/issues/852. rmw_zenoh failed to pass the test since the publisher declared in `test_async_sub` was accidentally detected by the subsequent `test_pub_sub` (the tests run in alphabetical order). The root cause is that the publisher node is not explicitly destroyed during the rclpy shutdown. 

To clarify, this behavior stems from the different mechanism used in rmw_zenoh compared to other DDS implementations. Specifically, the shutdown of rmw_zenoh doesn't immediately close the Zenoh session as long as other nodes are still alive. This aligns with the RMW philosophy that nodes and their associated entities such as publishers, subscriptions, and so on, are not explicitly destroyed by rmw_shutdown.

Introduing a sleep after `rclpy.shutdown` does not solve the issue because the node data remain referenced until the object destruction phase. Meanwhile, the next test begins immediately and reads the stale liveliness token, causing the test to fail.

This fix adotps the approach used in other tests by explicitly cleaning up the nodes to avoid such stale references.

author: garretrieger
body:
The merger prunes patch pairs from evaluation by looking at a "best case" cost reduction. During this calculation the size of the merged patch is estimated using the size of the individual patches being merged. The following forumula is used:

```
merged_size =
  largest_individual_patch_size +
  best_case_size_reduction_fraction * sum of remaining patch sizes
```

Setting best_case_size_reduction_fraction to 0 gives the previous behaviour, larger values cause more aggressive pruning, at the cost of possibly underestimating the true best case for a pair, and over pruning pairs that may have actually been viable.

Also adds a flag that when enabled has the merger record a histogram of encountered size reductions. This was used on a few example fonts to inform the default value of 0.50. In testing the default value gives a significant speedup, while having neglible impact on the total cost of produced segmentations.

author: copilot
body:
Implements `DELETE /v1/dish-reviews/:id/likes` to explicitly remove review likes, replacing the frontend's generic `toggleReaction` helper with direct API calls matching the ActionButtons pattern.

## Backend

- **Controller**: Added `DELETE /v1/dish-reviews/:id/likes` with OptionalJwtAuthGuard
- **Service**: Added `unlikeDishReview` - validates review existence, no notification on unlike
- **Repository**: Added `unlikeReview` using composite unique key `user_id_target_type_target_id_action_type`

## Frontend

**DishReviewsSection.tsx**: Replaced `toggleReaction` with explicit POST/DELETE via `callBackend`:

```typescript
// Before
await toggleReaction({
  target_type: "dish_reviews",
  target_id: reviewId,
  action_type: "like",
  willReact: willLike,
});

// After
if (willLike) {
  await callBackend(`v1/dish-reviews/${reviewId}/likes`, { method: "POST", requestPayload: {} });
} else {
  await callBackend(`v1/dish-reviews/${reviewId}/likes`, { method: "DELETE", requestPayload: {} });
}
```

Maintains instant UI feedback with error rollback, consistent with ActionButtons implementation.

@model function f()
    # ...

model = f()
opt_result = maximum_a_posteriori(model)
sample(model, NUTS(), 1000; initial_params=InitFromParams(opt_result))

author: mergify[bot]
body:
## Description

This closes https://github.com/ros2/rmw_zenoh/issues/852. rmw_zenoh failed to pass the test since the publisher declared in `test_async_sub` was accidentally detected by the subsequent `test_pub_sub` (the tests run in alphabetical order). The root cause is that the publisher node is not explicitly destroyed during the rclpy shutdown. 

To clarify, this behavior stems from the different mechanism used in rmw_zenoh compared to other DDS implementations. Specifically, the shutdown of rmw_zenoh doesn't immediately close the Zenoh session as long as other nodes are still alive. This aligns with the RMW philosophy that nodes and their associated entities such as publishers, subscriptions, and so on, are not explicitly destroyed by rmw_shutdown.

Introduing a sleep after `rclpy.shutdown` does not solve the issue because the node data remain referenced until the object destruction phase. Meanwhile, the next test begins immediately and reads the stale liveliness token, causing the test to fail.

This fix adotps the approach used in other tests by explicitly cleaning up the nodes to avoid such stale references.

body: ## Problem New users were immediately dropped into the products selection page without context about what PostHog can do for them. This made it harder for users to understand which products would help them achieve their goals. ## Changes ### New Use Case Selection Flow - Added a new `/onboarding/use-case` page where users select their primary goal before choosing products - Six use case options: - "Understand how users behave" → Product Analytics + Session Replay - "Find and fix issues" → Session Replay + Error Tracking - "Launch features with confidence" → Feature Flags + Experiments - "Collect user feedback" → Surveys + Product Analytics - "Monitor AI applications" → LLM Analytics - "I want to pick products myself" → Shows all products without pre-selection ### Enhanced Products Page - Pre-selects recommended products based on use case - Shows use case-based messaging when coming from use case selection - Added "Show all products" expandable section for discovering additional products - Improved card design with horizontal layout and descriptions for better scannability - Back button to change use case selection ### Feature Flag Integration - All redirects to `/products` now check `onboarding-use-case-selection` feature flag - When enabled, redirects to `/onboarding/use-case` instead - Consistent behavior across: - [sceneLogic.tsx:1125](frontend/src/scenes/sceneLogic.tsx#L1125) - Main onboarding redirect - [projectLogic.ts:137](frontend/src/scenes/projectLogic.ts#L137) - After creating new project - [organizationLogic.tsx:148](frontend/src/scenes/organizationLogic.tsx#L148) - After creating new organization - [ProjectNotice.tsx:88](frontend/src/layout/navigation/ProjectNotice.tsx#L88) - Demo project link ### Architecture - Created `productRecommendations.ts` as single source of truth for use case definitions - Added `UseCaseSelection.tsx` component with clean, accessible UI - Enhanced `productsLogic.ts` to handle URL params and pre-selection - Follows Kea patterns with proper separation of concerns ## How did you test this code? ### Automated Tests **Unit Tests:** - [frontend/src/scenes/products/productsLogic.test.ts](frontend/src/scenes/products/productsLogic.test.ts) - 15 tests covering product selection, use case preselection, URL handling, and onboarding navigation (all passing ✅) - [frontend/src/scenes/onboarding/useCaseSelection/useCaseSelectionLogic.test.ts](frontend/src/scenes/onboarding/useCaseSelection/useCaseSelectionLogic.test.ts) - 4 tests covering use case selection, analytics tracking, and different use case flows (all passing ✅) **E2E Tests:** - [playwright/e2e/onboarding-use-case-selection.spec.ts](playwright/e2e/onboarding-use-case-selection.spec.ts) - 11 comprehensive E2E tests covering full user flows **Storybook Stories:** - [frontend/src/scenes/onboarding/useCaseSelection/UseCaseSelection.stories.tsx](frontend/src/scenes/onboarding/useCaseSelection/UseCaseSelection.stories.tsx) -
